 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA) The Insurer is in appeal contending that the award of `5,30,020/- is incorrect on the premise that the death was not attributable to the injury suffered by the deceased in the accident.
2. The claimants are also in appeal contending that the sums awarded are inadequate.

3. As regards the argument that the death was not relatable to the injuries suffered by the deceased,
the medical records indicates that the victim of the incident Gurubasappa was hospitalized at Udayagiri Multi Specialty and Accident Hospital, Udgir between 21.12.2012 to 09.01.2013, during which period he was diagnosed with having an head injury due to the road traffic accident and he had altered sensorium with ischemic heart disease and diabetes mellitus (vide Ex.P.5).

entities.text: Udayagiri Multi Specialty and Accident Hospital, Udgir
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: NC: 2024:KHC-K:6848 4. Ex.P.6 - the discharge summary issued by the Narayana Hruduylaya - Mallareddy Hospital indicates that he was admitted in that hospital from 10.01.2013 to 02.02.2013 and he was referred to that hospital for further treatment.
It is stated that the chief complaints was of altered sensorium and not accepting anything orally.
The diagnosis of the hospital was an head injury due to a road traffic accident.

5. The summary of treatment indicates that after he was kept in the Intensive Care Unit and was treated conservatively and was in a stable condition, ambulatory and was tolerating diet and therefore was being discharged.
6. Gurubasappa was thereafter admitted to Siddharudh Charitable Hospital and Research Centre between 02.02.2013 to 12.03.2013.

entities.text: Siddharudh Charitable Hospital and Research Centre
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The discharge card indicates that he was brought to the hospital for a follow up treatment.

The next medical document available is Ex.P.9 issued by Sushruta Nursing Home, Bidar in which it is stated that Gurubasappa was diagnosed of Coronary artery disease (CAD), hypertension and he was admitted between 12.03.2013 to 29.03.2013.
The discharge card indicates that he had breathlessness, oedema of face, both legs and feet and discomfort in abdomen.

8. Thereafter for a period of five months there is no medical record and the next medical record available is Ex.P.10 of Mall Reddy Narayana Multispeciality Hospital, which indicates that he was admitted on 12.08.2013 and discharged on the same day.
The discharge summary indicates that he had a generalized body swelling and was not taking food orally since 15 days and he had a loss of appetite since 15 days.

sentences.text: This discharge summary does not indicate that the problem that he was suffering on 12.08.2013 was in any way relatable to his injuries suffered in a motor vehicle accident.
In fact, the said document states that on NC: 2024:KHC-K:6848 evaluation he was diagnosed as having hypoalbuminemia, hyponatremia and malnutrition and was advised for high protein and albumin diet.
It is stated that the patient was stable haemodynamically and was being discharged on request.
This document does not therefore indicate that any of his complaints was relatable to the injuries suffered by him.
10. It is not in dispute that thereafter on 24.08.2013 deceased Gurubasappa died.

In the light of the fact that between the period from March, 2013 to August, 2013 there is no document indicating the continuance of any ailments pursuant to the traffic accident and given the fact that Gurubasappa was 70 years as on the date of the accident, it cannot be concluded that the death was a result of the injury suffered by him in the accident.
To this extent, the finding of the Tribunal would be incorrect.

11. However, it is also to be noticed that from 21.12.2012 till the 29.03.2013 i.e., for nearly three NC:
2024:KHC-K:6848 months Gurubasappa was hospitalized continuously and this would indicate that he had suffered a serious head injury and was being treated at various hospitals.

In my view,
therefore having regard to the age of Gurubasappa i.e., 70 years, it would be appropriate to hold that he had suffered disability of 20%.
12. The accident occurred in the year 2012, the notional income of `6,500/- will have to be adopted as determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

13. As the deceased was aged 70 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121, a multiplier of '5' would have to be applied.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of `3,90,000/- (`6,500/- x 12 x '5') towards "loss of dependency" as against `1,60,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

Since the medical evidence on record itself indicates that Gurubsasppa was hospitalized for three months, i.e., 90 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum `1,00,000/- towards conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges.
The documentary evidence produced regarding medical evidence amounting to `2,50,000/- is affirmed.
15. The Gurubasappa having been hospitalized for nearly three months, it would be appropriate to award a sum of `75,000/- towards pain and suffering and `50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
16. A further sum of `42,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during laid-up period.

Consequently, in modification of the award of the Tribunal, the claimants are entitled to the following sums:
